# The negation of a round-up interval

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `upward_neg_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

A kernel of the round-up interval ([its kernels](upward.md)), of the opt-in header `kairn/upward.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include and which requires the options of [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md) (GCC and Clang `-frounding-math`, MSVC `/fp:strict`). No operation of it rounds: it gives the same result in every rounding mode.

## What it computes

A state of the round-up interval $Z = [-z_n, z_u]$ that contains $-x$ for every $x \in X$, with $X = [-x_n, x_u]$. An interval may be unbounded, and empty.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, -x : x \in X \,\}.$$

A state of the round-up interval is stored as its upper bound and its lower bound negated, the two lanes of one register: $X$ as $(x_u, x_n)$, $Z$ as $(z_u, z_n)$ ([its kernels](upward.md#the-stored-pair)).

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-X` | `upward::Interval<T>` | `upward::Interval<T>` | the two lanes exchanged; exact: does not round, the same result in every rounding mode; not `constexpr` |
| `neg(z, x)` | `upward::View<T>`, `upward::View<const T>` | `void` | a function on arrays, called by its qualified name (`kairn::upward::add` and the others): element by element on views of two plain arrays, the upper bounds and the negated lower bounds, with the kernel's form on arrays; it holds its own scope, so it may be called where the mode is to nearest; the views have the same length; `z` has, for each view read, the same two arrays (in place) or none that overlaps them, and its own two do not overlap ([The functions on arrays](../concepts/upward.md#the-functions-on-arrays)); not `constexpr` |
| `t - X` | `T`, `upward::Interval<T>` | `upward::Interval<T>` | $-(X + (-t))$, with [`upward_add_num_1`](upward_add_num_1.md): a composition through an exact negation, argued and not machine-checked as one statement ([What is not machine-checked](../concepts/correctness.md#what-is-not-machine-checked)); rounds upward: only inside an upward scope ([The scopes](../concepts/upward.md#the-scopes)); not `constexpr` |

`T` is `float` or `double`; `upward::Interval<T>` is the round-up interval `kairn::upward::Interval<T>`, `upward::View<T>` and `upward::View<const T>` the views of two arrays that the functions on arrays write and read, and `Interval<T, 1>` the default `kairn::Interval<T, 1>`. The operations are in namespace `kairn::upward`, header `kairn/upward.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include and which requires the options of [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md) (GCC and Clang `-frounding-math`, MSVC `/fp:strict`); an operation that rounds runs only inside an upward scope (a function on arrays holds its own). The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand (a function on arrays on its first input), which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X = [-x_n, x_u]$, stored as $(x_u, x_n)$, is a canonical state of the round-up interval: the empty set, both lanes a NaN; or a nonempty interval, each lane a number of `T` or $+\infty$ (neither a NaN nor $-\infty$), with $-x_n \le x_u$; its members are the real numbers between $-x_n$ and $x_u$.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **I1.** The result $Z = [-z_n, z_u]$, stored as $(z_u, z_n)$, is a canonical state of the round-up interval.
- **I2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when $X$ is.
- **I3.** $Z$ contains $-x$ for every $x \in X$, unbounded operands included (their members are real numbers).
- **I4.** For nonempty $X$, where $\ell$ and $h$ are the greatest lower bound and the least upper bound of the exact range $\{\, -x : x \in X \,\}$, as extended real numbers: $-z_n = \ell$ and $z_u = h$, exactly.
- **I5.** For bounded $X$, $Z$ is bounded exactly when every member $z$ of the exact range satisfies $\lvert z\rvert \le \Omega$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, no operation of the kernel rounding, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `upward_neg_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeUpwardArith.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeUpwardArith.v), against `upward_neg_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/UpwardStatements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/UpwardStatements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions upward_neg_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/UpwardAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/UpwardAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `upward_neg_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the two lanes exchanged (the listing of the round-up interval). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/upward_neg_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/upward_neg_1.kernel), the description the C++ (`include/kairn/gen/upward.hpp`) and the formal model (`proofs/gen/UpwardModel.v`) are generated from. Each statement is one operation of `T`, and none rounds to nearest ([the round-up interval in the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-round-up-interval)). A line of two statements separated by ` | ` is a *pair line*: the two lanes of one instruction, lane 0 on the left ([the pair form](../developer/design/upward.md#the-pair-form)).

```
# The negation of an interval of the round-up interval (docs/developer/design/upward.md, "Sum,
# difference, negation"): the two lanes exchanged, -[a, b] = [-b, -a] stored as (a, -b); exact, in
# every rounding mode; the empty set stays empty. Requires the rounding mode upward set by
# kairn::upward::Scope and the options of docs/concepts/upward.md (GCC and Clang -frounding-math,
# MSVC /fp:strict).

zu = copy(xn) | zn = copy(xu)                   # swap(x)
```

## Measured

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
- What the compiled code gives where its environment is not the one of the statement: no flush to zero of results or operands (its result does not depend on the rounding mode). That is the program's to make so, as [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md#what-the-program-guarantees) says, and no proof covers that step ([What is not machine-checked](../concepts/correctness.md#what-is-not-machine-checked)).
